runner.skillReadPolicy: If you choose to use an available skill, read its SKILL.md at the exact path in the available-skills inventory. Resolve each directly linked relative reference from that file. These rules apply to every benchmark file access, whether or not you use a skill. Use one simple read-only command at a time. The only pipeline you may use is `rg --files PATH... | rg REGEX`, with workspace paths and one non-option regex. Do not scan parent directories to discover skill files. Do not use any other pipeline, shell control chain, variable, loop, command substitution, redirection, or glob.

notes: Protocol version 5 retains the protocol-v4 qualification and identity chain. It permits only `rg --files PATH... | rg REGEX`, with existing readable producer paths inside the fixture workspace, direct zero-exit producer replay, and a single non-option consumer regex. Its routing observer uses case-normalized candidate-path identities. It does not rewrite earlier results.
All records and identifiers are synthetic. The benchmark must not access a real automation control plane.
Run paired comparisons only through scripts/run_behavior_benchmark.py so each arm uses an auth-only Codex home and allowlisted environment.
A direct Plugin Eval run provisions a local marketplace but does not establish the no-skill versus candidate-skills treatment used by the paired runner.
A completed Plugin Eval scenario is not a scored pass. The hidden oracle and runner score the final JSON separately.
The behavior benchmark measures read-only audit routing and proposition classification. It does not measure manage-skill activation or mutations.
Raw runs belong under the ignored development .benchmark directory, never under the runtime plugin tree.
